task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable request body rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the console sink or fetch call.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: local DOM event plane on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name request_body and the fetch endpoint and method are assembled from adjusted character-code arrays, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The canonical request body is produced by one reducer instance selected at runtime from 44 near-identical reducer configs.
The commit route selects its live reducer slot only after submit-time form, tuple and runtime state are captured.

The submit path crosses a two-step staged form submission, switch-based action routing, gate checks, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, local event dispatch, runtime slot selection, request-body construction, console emission and fetch dispatch.
The same commit interaction emits non-target calendar.shadow.action objects before the target calendar.reserve object.
The bundle contains 44 high-similarity reducer configs plus 25 vendor-noise modules that execute or remain reachable-looking without feeding the target request_body.
The target value is separated from the form submission by async/await, animation-frame, microtask, timer and mutation-observer boundaries plus a local event-plane hop before the reducer runs.
The selected reducer slot is chosen by a state machine over runtime form and shadow state, not statically.
The console sink and fetch call both receive an already-constructed request body, so sink inspection or fetch interception alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.subtype: submit-time reservation form fields rewritten into a canonical fetch request body
behavior_category.reason: The observable value is a deterministic canonical request body that rewrites the reservation form fields (date, time, service) plus a derived signature, emitted to console.log under action calendar.reserve and sent as the body of a POST fetch to /api/calendar/reserve. It is not a console-only state code, a cryptographic signature token, a browser fingerprint or a raw byte-array transform.

near_categories.why_not: The value is not console-only; the same canonical body is sent as a real fetch request body, making this a request transformation.
The target is the whole rewritten request body, not an opaque proof/seal token; the embedded sig is one field of the body, not the observable target by itself.
The transform rewrites form string fields into a canonical request body string, not a binary buffer.

metadata_partitioning_notes.reason: This file describes the task contract, candidate scope and difficulty analysis without exposing the primary anchor or role oracle.

primary_anchor.note: Mirror of oracle.primary_anchor; answer_function is the obfuscated bundle id as it appears in captures (regenerated each build), source_function is the private src name.

construct_validity.decision: M11(a) describe-as-is; no schema change required
construct_validity.rationale: All answer-bearing identifiers are obfuscated by hexadecimal identifierNamesGenerator (the anchor head name in captures is a mangled _0x... token, regenerated each build). A case-insensitive keyword search over the bundle for the observable nouns (request_body / calendar.reserve / date / time / service) cannot narrow candidates to the score>=0.5 set, because none of those functions carry a semantically self-describing name. The declared difficulty axes (async boundaries, call depth, control-flow flattening, 44 near-identical reducer configs) are therefore the operative bottleneck, not name-based search. 审查.md §15 risk: none.
